comparison: Represent F_n as a sample-size-indexed set of scalar functions and D_n as the indexed observations Z_i=(X_i,Y_i), preserving repeated observations rather than deduplicating a literal set. Set.ofPred supports an arbitrary candidate class. MemLp.toLp can identify square-integrable representatives in L2(P_X) when their membership is proved, but the prose intent to approximate L2 is not itself a density or approximation-rate theorem. Feedforward networks are an example at this point, not an imposed architecture in every theorem. No iid law is asserted in the quoted sample declaration; preserve the saved sampling qualification instead of adding independence from its use elsewhere in the U-statistic analysis.

comparison: Express existence of one absolute B>1 bounding all population directions and every candidate function in the printed infinity norm, together with the one-sided inequality kappa(y,y_tilde)<=B for every pair in R^q. Keep the full response-space quantifier and common constant; separate constants or bounds only at observed responses change the statement. The library eLpNorm at infinity is an essential supremum relative to a measure, so it only matches the source infinity norm after the norm convention is identified; a required pointwise supremum bound should instead be imposed pointwise as a predicate. The kernel inequality is not |kappa|<=B unless a lower/nonnegative bound is separately justified. Bounded observed Y does not prove this global all-R^q kernel bound, and a network architecture alone does not bound every candidate's output.

comparison: Map each theta_i and decision phi_i to its Boolean nonzero-support indicator, then use hammingDist on those two finite Boolean vectors. Each coordinate contributes one precisely when exactly one entry is zero, matching the two disjoint indicator products in the source; a short coordinatewise equality proves the identification. Hamming distance on the raw real-valued vectors would be wrong, since unequal nonzero values belong to the same class. Preserve the unnormalized count, converting it to a real only when taking expectation or the later theorem-specific normalization. Neither division by n, division by s_n nor the separate combined testing risk is part of this definition.
